name: Fabricated chutes, gates, tripper structures & skirts
why: Fabricated steel with liners. TPL has an established structural fabricator panel and its own steel cost model. Free-issue plate option available.
basis: Fabrication conversion tendered direct; plate and liner supplied free-issue or on TPL rate contract.
vendors: TPL structural fabricator panel; Pennar Industries; SEW Infrastructure fabrication; regional Nagpur / Raipur / Bhilai fabricators. Liners: Tega Industries, Sandvik wear, Hardox distributors.
sourcing: Tender fabrication conversion on Rs/T. Consider free-issue plate on the TPL steel rate contract to strip a second margin layer.

name: Conveyor belting (NN + steel cord)
why: Highly liquid market with published Rs/m benchmarks. OEM adds a trading margin only. Direct contracting with belt manufacturers is standard practice.
basis: Trading margin only. Benchmark against published Rs/m rates once the belt schedule is received.
vendors: Forech India; Oriental Rubber Industries; ContiTech / Phoenix Conveyor Belt; Fenner Conveyor Belting (Michelin); MRF Muscleflex; Bando India; TEGA.
sourcing: Single tender for NN and steel cord together. Benchmark on Rs/m by width, ply and cover grade once the belt schedule is received.

name: Idlers & idler frames
why: Competitive Indian manufacturer base. Repeat-buy commodity for TPL across coal handling projects.
basis: Competitive manufacturer base. Validate against recent TPL idler POs before finalising.
vendors: TRF Ltd; Elecon Engineering; Tega Industries; Bevcon Wayors; Sandvik; Rulmeca India; Ashoka Rollers.
sourcing: Club with Lot 6 for volume leverage. Validate against recent TPL idler POs on other coal handling jobs.

name: Technological structure incl. stringers
why: Plain fabricated structure. Highest single-lot margin release. Run through the TPL structural steel cost model before tendering.
basis: Rs 1,75,000/T against TPL structural steel cost model. Highest confidence band pending that run.
vendors: TPL structural fabricator panel; Pennar Industries; Interarch; Kirby Building Systems; regional heavy fabricators.
sourcing: Run through the TPL structural steel cost model before tendering. Highest single-lot release in the package.

name: Drive train (motors, gearboxes, couplings, brakes)
why: Branded proprietary components bought out by the OEM and passed through with a handling load. TPL buys HT/LT motors directly on other packages.
basis: Branded pass-through. HT motor at Rs 7.50 Cr is the single largest sub-line.
vendors: Motors: ABB, Siemens, CG Power, Kirloskar Electric, WEG, BHEL. Gearboxes: Elecon, Premium Transmission, Flender (Siemens), Radicon, Shanthi Gears. Couplings: Fluidomat, Voith Turbo, Premium, Elecon. Brakes: EMCO Dynatorq, Ferrotech.
sourcing: Split into three sub-enquiries. HT motor at Rs 7.50 Cr equivalent is the largest sub-line and should ride on any existing TPL motor rate contract.

name: Pulleys & deflector rollers
why: Competitive manufacturer base, same vendors as idlers. Can be clubbed with Lot 3 for volume leverage.
basis: Same vendor base as idlers. Club Lots 3 and 6 for volume leverage.
vendors: TRF Ltd; Elecon Engineering; Bevcon Wayors; Tega Industries; Sandvik.
sourcing: Club with Lot 3. Lagging specification (rubber / ceramic) drives the rate and must be frozen before enquiry.

name: Electrical & C&I bought-outs
why: TPL already procures cables, trays, conduit and switchgear centrally under rate contracts. Largest percentage release in the package.
basis: Buy on existing TPL cable, tray and conduit rate contracts. Largest percentage release.
vendors: Cables: Polycab, KEI, Havells, Finolex, RR Kabel, Apar. Trays and conduit: existing TPL panel. Switches: Procon, Techno Instruments, Schmersal, Flexicon, Pepperl+Fuchs. Actuators: Rotork, AUMA, L&T Valves.
sourcing: Route entirely through existing TPL rate contracts. Coordinate with the Electrical category lead; at Anuppur most of this already sits in the Electrical and C&I budgets.

name: Mandatory spares
why: Follows the parent lots. Buy from the same direct vendors at the same negotiated rates.
basis: Follows parent lots at the parent negotiated rates.
vendors: Same vendors as the parent lots.
sourcing: Negotiate spares pricing inside each parent lot order rather than as a separate tender.

name: Magnetics & detection
why: Branded bought-out instruments. Narrow specialist vendor base, direct contracting straightforward.
basis: Narrow specialist base. Limited competitive tension caps the release.
vendors: Magnets and ILMS: Electro Flux Equipments, Jupiter Magnetics, Star Trace, Eriez India. Metal detectors: Mesutronic, Loma, Electro Flux, Eriez. Belt weighers: Schenck Process, Thermo Ramsey, Transweigh India.
sourcing: Narrow specialist base. Expect limited competitive tension; negotiate on the back of multi-project volume.

name: Bearings, plummer blocks & adapter sleeves
why: Pure branded pass-through. Buy direct from bearing manufacturers or authorised distributors.
basis: Direct from bearing manufacturer or authorised distributor.
vendors: SKF India; Schaeffler (FAG); Timken India; NBC (National Engineering); Rollway. Housings: SKF SNL / SAF, Dodge, Cooper split.
sourcing: 408 bearing assemblies. Buy direct from manufacturer or authorised distributor. Freeze the bearing schedule by pulley type first; the BBU flat rate hides genuine size variation.

name: Scrapers, conveyor misc & vulcaniser
why: Small value. Club with Lot 3 or Lot 6 rather than running a separate tender.
basis: Small value. Club with Lot 3 or 6.
vendors: Scrapers: Tega, Flexco, Martin Engineering India, ASGCO, Brelko. Vulcaniser: Shaw Almex, Nilos, Forech.
sourcing: Small value. Club with Lot 3 or Lot 6 rather than a standalone tender.

name: Coal sampling units
why: KEEP BUNDLED. High engineering content, low value (1.1% of package). Interface risk on sampling accuracy outweighs the margin release.
vendors: Elecon Engineering; Bevcon Wayors; TRF Ltd; Tega Industries.
sourcing: KEEP BUNDLED with the D&I contractor. Sampling accuracy is a guaranteed parameter and should not be split.
